components: the three-run ள form written over its baseline
strokeOrder: write உ first: sweep outward around its compact upper spiral
without lifting, descend through its broad outer curve and turn left onto the baseline
without lifting, carry the long baseline straight to the right — then lift once
write ள over that base: curl around its added left loop
without lifting, turn inward through the loop
without lifting, descend around its inner curl — then lift a second time
set the pen at the bottom of the adjoining upright and draw upward
without lifting, carry the top bar to the right — then lift a third time
set the pen at the top of the separate right upright and draw straight down
strokeOrderNote: four strokes — first write the three joined movements of உ, then add ள in its familiar three-run order (joined movements 1–3, joined 4–5, and separate 6); cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Module 17 with Appendix I Frames 17, 16, and 12

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Module 17, ஊ construction, with Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frames 17, 16, and 12 (University of Texas at Austin), pp. 195–196
strokeOrderSource.variation: Module 17 identifies ஊ as long ū and explicitly constructs it from two familiar letters: write உ first, then write ள over it. Appendix I Frame 16 keeps உ's three movements joined, while Frame 12 groups ள's six movements into three pen-down runs. The resulting four-run learner order is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil ஊ outline; Tamil handwriting varies by school.

notes: Independent long ū opens words such as ஊர் (ūr, native place) and ஊசி (ūsi, needle). The manual teaches the letter compositionally: write short உ first, then overlay the already learned ள form.
